Cautiously positive, but the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a softer credit backdrop than the FOMC statement alone implies. While the Fed notes strong labor markets, solid growth, and inflation near 2 percent with a “patient” stance, SLOOS indicates:
- Banks tightened standards and/or other terms on C&I and construction/land development loans, with wider loan rate spreads and concerns about collateral values.
- Weaker reported demand for business loans, residential real estate loans, HELOCs, and construction lending.
- Expectations for 2019 leaned toward tighter standards for C&I and CRE and weaker business loan demand, alongside anticipated deterioration in mortgage and nonprime consumer loan performance.
- Some consumer categories showed unchanged standards (e.g., GSE-eligible mortgages, HELOCs, auto), tempering the downside.

These credit conditions and demand signals temper the optimism in the January 2019 statement, nudging the tone more cautious than previously assessed.
